title: Comparing Numbers: More, Fewer or the Same
seo_title: Kindergarten Comparing Numbers Worksheets: More, Fewer, Same, Greater and Less
standard_text: Identify whether the number of objects in one group is greater than, less than, or equal to the number of objects in another group, e.g., by using matching and counting strategies.
meta_desc: Free kindergarten comparing numbers worksheets: match two groups one to one, find more, fewer or the same, pick the box with the most or fewest, and compare numbers 1 to 10 (greater and less). 100 picture questions with an answer key.
key_big: Match one to one. The group with some left over has more.
key_sub: When you count, the number that comes later is greater. A longer row is not always more.
body_html:
Match one to one

Put each thing in one row with a thing in the other row. The row with things left over has more. The other row has fewer.

If nothing is left over, they are the same number.

A longer row is not always more

Compare numbers

When you count, the number that comes later is greater. The number that comes first is less.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do
Thinking a longer row has moreMatch or count the things
Mixing up more and fewerMore has things left over
Saying 3 is greater than 5Count: 5 comes after 3, so 5 is greater

faq.q: What does comparing numbers mean in kindergarten?
faq.a: Children look at two groups and say which has more, which has fewer, or if they are the same. They also compare written numbers from 1 to 10, like 7 and 4.

faq.q: Why does my child think a spread-out row has more?
faq.a: Young children often judge by how long a row looks. Line the things up one to one, or count both rows, to show that the number does not change when things are spread out.

faq.q: How can I practice at home?
faq.a: Set the table: is there one spoon for each plate? Compare snacks, toy cars or blocks. Ask: Who has more? How do you know?

faq.q: Should kindergartners use the signs > and <?
faq.a: Not yet. In kindergarten children use the words greater, less, more, fewer and the same. The signs come in Grade 1.
